findings.issue_text: Adding abstract order() breaks binary compatibility with existing third-party CryptoProvider implementations, causing AbstractMethodError during provider discovery
Equal crypto-provider priorities are resolved by ServiceLoader encounter order, allowing non-deterministic selection of non-FIPS crypto when FIPS and default providers coexist
getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the provider for the JVM default keystore type rather than Bouncy Castle/FIPS, which can select the wrong JCA provider and fail for BC-only algorithms

goldens.comment: Returns wrong provider (default keystore instead of BouncyCastle)

Dead code exists where ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded. The actual encoding is performed by new ASN1Encoder instances created in the subsequent return statement, rendering the earlier operations useless.
When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
Abstract order() method on CryptoProvider may break backward compatibility with existing implementations

adjudication_records.issue_text: Equal crypto-provider priorities are resolved by ServiceLoader encounter order, allowing non-deterministic selection of non-FIPS crypto when FIPS and default providers coexist

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims equal priorities cause non-deterministic selection, but the diff shows distinct priority values: AuthzClientCryptoProvider has order() returning 100, while DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return 200. The sorting in CryptoIntegration uses Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order).reversed(), meaning higher order values are preferred. With these distinct values (200 vs 100), the selection is deterministic - the 200-priority providers will always be selected over the 100-priority AuthzClientCryptoProvider. There is no scenario in the diff where FIPS and default providers have equal priorities.
